title: Rollout onboarding tour for first-time users – prototype feedback & accessibility polish
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description: Design an in-console guided onboarding tour for users creating their first rollout. Scope includes a lightweight stepper overlay that introduces the rollout timeline, canary vs full rollout choice, cost impact preview, and keyboard-accessible failure-recovery tips. The goal is to reduce initial setup confusion for new PMs and SREs, lower support tickets for 'where did my rollout go', and improve first-time success rate when creating rollouts. Deliverables: Figma interactive prototype (desktop + tablet), accessibility checklist, microcopy bank for each step, handoff tokens and redlines for engineering. This ticket covers the main prototype iteration and stakeholder review cycle; follow-ups (analytics tracking, localization) will be separate tickets.
comments: 2025-02-14 Sofia Nguyen: Initial upload of prototype v0.1. Focused on minimal modal with 4 steps: (1) purpose + benefits, (2) select variant (canary vs full), (3) preview cost & SLO tradeoffs, (4) recovery & links to docs. Uploaded Figma and included microcopy suggestions. Requested PM + Eng review.

2025-02-15 Diego Patel (PM): High-level thumbs up. Ask: can we surface recent anomalies alongside cost preview so users can make informed decisions? Suggest adding an optional 'show recent errors' toggle in step 3. Please validate with engineering on data latency for anomaly fetch.

2025-02-16 Marie Chen (Engineering): Feasibility note: pulling real-time anomaly list has perf implications; recommend showing a one-line summary and link to incidents instead of live list. Also raised concern about overlay blocking autosave prompts in the rollout editor — flagged as blocker to resolve before deploy.

2025-02-18 Accessibility Review (R. Ahmed): Keyboard flows mostly ok; focus order for the stepper needs fixes. Color contrast for the highlight pill is borderline at 3.9:1 — suggested darker accent or outline. Added step to include ARIA live region for success/error toast in step 4.

2025-02-20 Ava Morgan (Designer, assignee): Updated prototype v0.2 with reduced anomaly detail (one-line summary + link), adjusted focus order, and darker accent token. Added 'Skip tour' and 'Remind me later' options; documented telemetry events for each action. Uploaded revised Figma and a 2-minute walkthrough recording.

2025-02-22 Product Review (S. Kapoor): Stakeholders liked the 'cost preview' card but requested clearer language around billing impact — suggested changing 'approx tokens' to 'estimated monthly cost' and adding a learn-more link to pricing. Also asked to surface a 'recommended default' for canary percent with rationale.

2025-02-24 Engineering Handoff (L. Ortiz): Requested explicit redlines for spacing and tokenized color variables. Also flagged a corner case: when the console is in narrow density mode the overlay should collapse into an anchored help bubble. Added this as follow-up constraint for implementation.

2025-02-25 QA observation (J. Ramos): During internal playtest, the keyboard shortcut to advance steps conflicted with existing console shortcut (g). Proposed remap to Right Arrow + Enter only. Also noted a missing localization key for the 'Skip tour' copy.

2025-02-26 Sofia Nguyen: Collated feedback and uploaded prototype v0.3 (addressing a11y, microcopy, and eng redlines). Requesting final sign-off from PM + Eng before we schedule dev spike. Planned follow-up tickets for analytics, localization, and narrow-density behavior.
decisions: Keep onboarding opt-out by default (user must explicitly start tour) to avoid interrupting power users.
Anomaly details replaced with a one-line summary plus link to incidents to avoid perf issues.
Show recommended canary percent (default 10%) with contextual rationale copy written for product.
Accessibility fixes required before implementation: fix focus order, increase contrast for highlight pill to 4.5:1, add ARIA live region for toasts.
Narrow density mode: collapse overlay to anchored help bubble — implementation to be scoped as separate follow-up.
